notes:
Account summary: Enterprise insurance platform (policy servicing + claims). Heavy seasonal peaks (renewal window) — requires predictable throughput for parallel chat sessions and claim reranking. Interested in Redwood Dedicated to eliminate noisy neighbor risk and to support VPC-only deployment.

POC objective: Validate Dedicated capacity sizing to meet latency SLOs (95th <= 120ms for chat token generation under 10k concurrent sessions), verify sustained throughput (tokens/s), and exercise failover/fallback policies. Also verify quantization tradeoffs for cost reduction w/o quality regression.

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2026-01-14: Initial inbound via website form; AE assigned (Priya).
- 2026-01-22: Discovery call — confirmed need for vpc + audit logs; gathered baseline traffic patterns (peak concurrent chat ~8k, avg session length 220 tokens). Action: SE to propose GPU count. (Marcus)
- 2026-02-05: NDA signed; security questionnaire requested. Drive: Security_FAQ_responses.docx linked.
- 2026-02-18: Technical kickoff (Fireflies FF-20260218-0041). SE proposed 12xA10G per Dedicated pool as starting point (estimate).
- 2026-02-26: Load test plan agreed — mixture of representative prompts (support chat, claim-summary, reranking of 50 candidates). Test dataset provided by PulseForge (redacted).
- 2026-03-03: First load run (FF-20260303-0098). Observations: steady-state throughput ~72% of target; tail latency at 95th spiked to ~210ms under synthetic worst-case prompt length. Ticket INF-4319 opened to investigate kernel selection + batch sizing.
- 2026-03-05: SE updated config: increased batching cap, enabled prefix caching for common prompts, adjusted routing to prefer dedicated pool per region. Follow-up soak scheduled.
- 2026-03-08: Soak test (6 hours) in region us-east-1 completed. Sustained throughput held at ~90% of required. Noted periodic GC stalls on older runtime nodes; escalation to infra. INF-4387 created.

Technical details / requirements:
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile token generation <= 120ms for short chat prompts (<=64 tokens). 99th percentile <= 300ms preferred.
- Throughput target: sustain 60M tokens/hour during renewal peaks (approx. 10k concurrent chat sessions).
- Model prefs: prefer Llama2-70B/Redwood-rl variant for reranking + chat; open to quantized 4-bit variants if quality validated.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial POC target = 12 GPUs (A10G equiv); aiming to confirm final commit of 24 GPUs for peak months with autoscaling burst. Need per-GPU tokens/sec measured in POC to finalize.
- Failure modes tested: node OOM, node reboot, region failover; automatic fallback to smaller model in adjacent region acceptable for short intervals.

POC results highlight:
- Pros: Dedicated removes noisy neighbor variability; prefix caching yields 18% token cost reduction for common flows; batching increases effective throughput w/ acceptable quality.
- Cons: Tail latency needs work — 95th still above target for worst-case long prompts; runtime kernel mismatch on some nodes causing periodic latency spikes.

Open action items / next steps (short):
- SE (Marcus) to run focused kernel/quantization benchmark matrix by 2026-03-18.
- Infra to replace older runtime instances in pool; retest soak. Target: 2026-03-22.
- Legal to clear data residency clause and review SLA language around latency SLO credits. Target: procurement meeting 2026-03-29.
- Schedule executive demo and walk-through of cost model (Priya) after soak pass.

Notes from procurement/security call (3/3):
- PulseForge procurement: wants explicit throughput guarantees and a clear overage pricing model for burst. "We need predictability or we won't commit to 12-month reserved" (quote paraphrase).
- Security requested HSM/KMS attestations for key wrapping; Redwood to provide KMS integration notes (Drive link).

Short-term blockers: legal SLA wording, final GPU per-region mapping, tail latency investigation.

CRM culture notes: Entered a lot of shorthand in threads; PulseForge likes concrete numbers and runbooks — pushed to include a short runbook for on-call infra steps in POC deliverables.

Relevant artifacts:
- POC plan: drive:/PulseForge/Redwood_Dedicated_POC_plan_v1.pptx
- Test results workbook: drive:/PulseForge/Latency_SLOs_and_Test_Results.xlsx
- Open tickets: INF-4319 (kernel/batch tuning), INF-4387 (runtime node upgrade)

Recommended Redwood playbook:
- Offer a 4-week trial SLA addendum tied to POC perf targets (95th <= 140ms, throughput >= 85% target) with credits; helps procurement commit to reserve sizing.
- Provide a quantified kernel & quantization report showing expected token/sec per GPU across variants.
- Propose a hybrid reserved+burst model: base reserved for 24/7 baseline, autoscale burst for renewal windows with cost cap.

Bottom line: Product fit strong. Main risk is agreeing explicit latency/throughput SLAs and confirming final per-GPU throughput to set a firm reserved commit. POC needs two more cycles (kernel tuning + upgraded runtime nodes) before recommending procurement commit.
